prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The scene is an indoor room with a flat wall directly ahead (~1.0–1.5 m away), a doorway on the right (~1.5 m away), a cluttered bin of objects (including a unicorn mask, books like 'Hamilton' and 'Infinity Gauntlet', and bags) below and in front (~0.4–1.0 m away), and a standing man who appears on the right in frame 5 (~1.0–1.2 m away, roughly 0.5 m to the right of the bin). Across the five frames, the camera wearer steps back slightly and pans right from the bin (closest at ~0.3–0.6 m in frame 1) toward the doorway as the man enters on the right in frame 5, facing forward/left toward the camera wearer and the bin with his upper head cropped out of view and his outstretched right hand within arm's reach (~0.3 m) of a brown bag below him, while the bin remains within or just at the edge of the camera wearer's reach (~0.7–1.0 m). The depth map clearly separates the protruding 3D silhouettes of the upright books, unicorn horn, and the man's torso and extended right arm from the background wall in frames 4 and 5, which is harder to gauge from the flat lighting in the RGB image. However, the per-frame normalized monocular depth is highly unreliable on the featureless yellow wall—inverting its gradient across frames and rendering the background wall bright white (near) in frame 3—and produces an erroneous bright-white artifact above the man's right shoulder in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: In the indoor scene containing a lower-left/center bin of books, bags, and a unicorn mask (~0.4–1.0 m away) in front of a wall (~1.0–1.5 m away), the segmentation map isolates only two foreground regions labeled 'person' while leaving the background wall, doorway, and objects in the middle frames completely unsegmented on black. In frame 5, it accurately outlines the standing man on the right (~1.0–1.2 m from the camera wearer and ~0.5 m right of the bin), whose torso faces left/forward toward the camera wearer while his upper head is occluded by the top frame edge and his right hand reaches down within arm's reach of a brown paper bag. Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera retreats slightly from the bin and turns right toward the doorway, the map shows a mask in the lower left of frame 1 (~0.3–0.6 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach), nothing in frames 2–4 where the bin sits low in the frame, and the entering man on the right in frame 5. While the frame 5 mask provides a sharp boundary separating the man's dark-sleeved arms and torso from the shadowed doorway behind him that blends together in RGB, the map is unreliable in frame 1 where it falsely classifies the cluttered pile of inanimate objects (the unicorn mask, horn, and cloth) as a 'person', and it fails to segment any of the individual books, bags, or containers across the sequence.
descriptions.pose: Within the room where a bin of objects sits below in the foreground (~0.4–1.0 m away) and a man stands on the right in front of a doorway (~1.0–1.2 m from the camera wearer and ~0.5 m from the bin), the pose map is completely blank across frames 1–4 and renders skeletons only in the lower-right corner of frame 5 as the camera turns right and the man enters view. In frame 5, two magenta hand skeletons accurately localize the man's right hand extending forward and downward—fingers spread and within arm's reach of the brown bag below—and his left hand positioned lower near his waist at the bottom-right frame boundary. Whereas the man's upper body in RGB clearly faces angled toward the camera wearer and the bin with his eyes and upper head cropped out by the top border, the yellow body skeleton fails to capture his actual shoulders, neck, or torso. The pose map makes the exact finger articulation and open-palm orientation of the man's motion-blurred right hand much clearer than in the RGB frame, but it is severely unreliable for body pose: it completely misses the man's upper-body skeleton and instead hallucinates a tiny, compressed yellow body skeleton clustered directly beside his right wrist.
